tools.name: best_card_for_purchase
tools.description: Which card earns the most rewards for a purchase, and why. With no cards given and no saved wallet, it ranks every card earnrate knows (in `allCards`): a complete answer for anyone. With cards named in the conversation (`cards`) or a saved wallet, it picks the best of the user's own: `decision.cardId` is the pick and `decision.checkoutLabel` is how the card appears at checkout, with every usable card ranked with reasons, cards the merchant won't take, assumptions, warnings, and when a different point valuation would change the pick. For a business earnrate may not know, like a local restaurant, pass `category` when you can tell what kind of business it is. Never needs or returns card numbers.

tools.name: compare_welcome_offers
tools.description: Ranks the public welcome (sign-up) offers on cards the user doesn't have by first-year value: the bonus at the user's point values minus the first year's annual fee and any membership the card needs that the user doesn't have. Offers the issuer rules out because of a card in the user's wallet are marked likely not eligible and listed last. Use it when the user asks which new card to get or which has the best sign-up bonus. It covers only the cards earnrate knows, offers vary by person, and each offer's note gives the issuer's eligibility rules; pass those caveats on. It doesn't account for what a card would earn on the user's spending.

tools.description: Finds credit cards in earnrate's catalog by name or issuer, e.g. "sapphire", "amex gold" or "bofa". Returns each card's id (for add_card), network, annual fee, whether it's already in the wallet, and what it needs set up: category picks and their options, memberships, activations. Leave the query out to list every card. US cards only.

tools.name: record_purchase
tools.description: Records a purchase the user has already made, so spending caps and welcome-bonus progress stay accurate for future recommendations. It updates the user's saved wallet. Only call it after the purchase has happened, and only once per purchase: calling it twice counts the spend twice. Purchases with no cap and no open welcome bonus are acknowledged and nothing is written. For a merchant earnrate doesn't recognize it asks for category first, so caps aren't missed.

instructions:
earnrate answers which credit card earns the most for a purchase, from each issuer's own terms. Anyone can use it without entering anything: with no cards given, best_card_for_purchase, best_cards_for, cheat_sheet, simulate_spending and compare_welcome_offers answer from every card earnrate knows, and that's a complete answer. Never require the user's cards, and don't ask what they spend unless the answer depends on it; simulate_spending assumes typical amounts when none are given and says so.

Personalizing is optional. If the user names their cards, pass them as `cards` (ids from search_cards) for that answer; nothing is saved. After answering, offer once to save those cards so earnrate remembers them, and save them with add_card only if the user says yes. Only if they want earnrate to remember their cards, track spending caps or welcome bonuses, or record purchases, save a wallet with add_card and the other wallet tools. When a card needs category picks, memberships like Amazon Prime, or activations, ask the user rather than guessing.

The wallet lists cards by product id, never card numbers; never ask for card numbers, expiry dates or security codes.
